observations.text: SP, due to insufficient directional control technique with the rudder during the take off roll, did not maintain the A/C at the centerline of the RWY, with the result of a lateral displacement of 15 ft toward the RWY edge. The IP had to intervene on the controls to re-establish the take off run on the centerline. Correction of the take off roll technique is required before the next instrument sortie.

SP, due to an attention bottleneck on a single caution indication at the expense of the instrument cross-check, did not bring the A/C to the proper T/O attitude and delayed the rotation, with the result that the lift-off occurred 16 knots above the calculated take off airspeed. The IP had to direct the rotation and the establishment of the climbing attitude. Distribution of attention between the cockpit indications and the primary flight instruments is to be reviewed in the brief.

SP, due to a late and shallow control input at rotation, did not execute the T/O with the standard airspeed, with the result that the lift-off occurred 10 knots above the calculated take off airspeed, at the limit of the allowed tolerance. The deviation was recognized with delay and the proper climbing attitude was established only after the IP's verbal prompts. No intervention on the controls was required.

SP, due to distraction from the primary scan by an unrelated switch action after brakes release, did not maintain the A/C at the centerline during the take off roll, with the result of a lateral deviation of 10 ft, at the limit of the allowed tolerance. The drift was recognized with delay and was corrected only after the IP's verbal prompt. Sequencing of the cockpit actions after brakes release is to be re-briefed.

SP executed the take off within the desired standards, performing the LINE UP checks without omissions and cleaning the A/C configuration without violating the speed limit. However, the lift-off occurred 9 knots above the calculated take off airspeed and the lateral deviation from the centerline reached 9 ft, both recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. Marginal performance for the Training Section - closer control of the rotation airspeed and of centerline tracking is expected to improve on the following sorties.

SP executed the take off with accuracy and speed, maintaining the A/C at the centerline within 3 ft and lifting off within 3 knots of the calculated take off airspeed. The proper T/O and climbing attitudes were established and maintained, the L/G and flaps were retracted without violating the speed limit, and the After Takeoff Checklist was completed without omissions and without IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the take off with exceptional accuracy, above the desired levels for the Training Section, holding the A/C on the centerline within 1 ft and lifting off within 1 knot of the calculated take off airspeed. The A/C performance checks against the calculated T/O data, the acceleration to the standard climb airspeed and the transition to the primary flight instruments were carried out in an impeccable and standardized manner, with no prompting from the IP. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to incorrect application of the crosswind correction during the take off roll, did not maintain the A/C at the centerline of the RWY, with the result of a lateral displacement of 14 ft toward the downwind edge. The IP had to take the controls to re-establish the take off run. The take off roll technique is to be re-briefed and demonstrated before the next sortie.

SP, due to a checklist not followed correctly (AE102) before takeoff, did not execute the LINE UP checks without omissions and commenced the take off roll with the A/C not configured as briefed. The IP had to direct the omitted items and part of the departure sequence, and the lift-off occurred 13 knots above the calculated take off airspeed. Further study of the Line Up and After Takeoff checklists is required.

SP, due to a non-standard rotation technique with an insufficient initial pitch rate, did not bring the A/C to the proper T/O attitude at the standard airspeed, with the result that the lift-off occurred 10 knots above the calculated take off airspeed, at the limit of the allowed tolerance. The deviation was recognized with delay and the climbing attitude was established only after the IP's verbal prompts, without intervention on the controls.

SP, due to an interrupted cross-check between the outside references and the primary flight instruments during the take off roll, did not maintain the A/C at the centerline, with the result of a lateral deviation of 10 ft, at the limit of the allowed tolerance. The drift was recognized with delay and was corrected only after the IP's verbal prompt, with no intervention on the controls required.

SP, due to a late and oversized rudder correction at the start of the take off roll, did not maintain the A/C at the centerline with the required accuracy, with the result of a lateral deviation of 7 ft. The deviation was minor and was recognized and corrected in a timely manner, without IP's intervention. Rudder inputs after brakes release are to be applied earlier and in smaller increments.

SP, due to poor workload distribution, with the departure clearance read-back handled during the take off roll, did not rotate at the standard airspeed, with the result that the lift-off occurred 8 knots above the calculated take off airspeed. The error was minor and was recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention, the proper climbing attitude being established immediately afterwards.

SP executed the take off within the desired standards, performing the LINE UP checks without omissions, maintaining the A/C at the centerline within 4 ft and lifting off within 4 knots of the calculated take off airspeed. Both parameters, however, remained close to the outer edge of the accuracy required for this Training Section, and the climbing attitude was established with a small delay after the L/G retraction. Marginal performance for the Training Section - tighter control of the rotation airspeed and of centerline tracking is expected to improve on the following instrument sorties.

SP demonstrated exceptional accuracy on the take off, above the desired levels for this Training Section, with the A/C held on the centerline within 1 ft throughout the roll and the lift-off within 1 knot of the calculated take off airspeed. The engine run-up was completed with no movement of the A/C, the configuration was cleaned well inside the speed limit, and the After Takeoff Checklist and the transition to the primary flight instruments were carried out without any prompting from the IP. Above end of block MIF achieved.
